text: {"headline":"Elevated 99215 use across every complexity tier, including many 0–1 condition patients, points toward possible upcoding, but records for only one 99215 claim leave the documentation side untested.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The billing pattern leans toward upcoding. The provider's 99215 share runs well above the all-provider share in every complexity tier, not only among sicker patients. The sampled low-complexity 99215 claims include single-problem or symptom-only visits, such as C0081769 (R10.9, no chronic conditions) and repeat 99215s for patient M0034588 (C0081968, C0082091, C0082264) on rash and upper respiratory diagnoses. The billing is also heavily concentrated at 99214, which warrants a look of its own. The documentation cannot confirm or refute any of this: only one 99215 claim (C0082071) had records, and it supported the billed level, while the 12 documented 99214 claims all matched, so the records are too thin to judge whether the high-level codes are supported. A reviewer should first request charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims, prioritizing patient M0034588 and the 0-condition visits, and check whether the MDM and time in those notes genuinely support high complexity or read as templated."}
